mission: Arrival at the next survey point, which is not a ruin. The structure has power, a Force-recognition mechanism calibrated for an older era, and a warning message that has been broadcasting on a dead frequency for centuries.
why_now: The bearing lands them on a world that should not carry a functioning Jedi installation. It does. The survey mission now has infrastructure on the other end of it.
conflict: The facility's Force-recognition mechanism scans Ben and grudgingly accepts him — as if it was designed for practitioners whose signature does not quite match his. Something older in his lineage triggers the admit. Desh's instruments say this building should not still be running, and it is.
turning_point: Automated systems wake, cycling a centuries-old warning through dead frequencies until it resolves into archaic Basic: two words, SEAL FAILING.
opening_hook: The structure isn't ruins. It has power.
closing_hook: The message resolves into Basic — archaic but readable. Two words: 'SEAL FAILING.'
emotional_trajectory: Cautious exploration -> growing awe -> sharp alarm

stakes.personal: Ben is standing in front of something the modern Jedi Order does not know exists
stakes.interpersonal: Desh's professional assessment shifts from 'interesting survey find' to 'threat assessment'
stakes.external: An ancient Jedi military installation has been broadcasting a distress signal no one has heard

setting: Unnamed Outer Rim world — the perimeter facility, partially underground, Jedi Lords-era construction
sensory_details: Humming power cells; dust on consoles that have not been touched in centuries; the wrongness denser here, close-pressure under the sternum rather than ambient; Desh's chrono running two seconds fast against Ben's
canon_elements_needed: Jedi Lords era military infrastructure and construction
Ancient Jedi Force-recognition technology and bio-locks
Pre-Ruusan Reformation Jedi Order military operations
action_beats: Ben and Desh approach the powered facility on foot across barren terrain, blasters holstered but hands near grips
The facility's Force-recognition mechanism scans Ben with a blue pulse of light that crawls across his body
Automated systems activate — displays flickering to life, centuries-old warning message cycling through dead frequencies
Desh draws his sidearm and sweeps the entry corridor while Ben reads the warning resolving into Basic
promises_planted: The seal failure has a hard timeline (PP24)
The primary wound site will be physically visited (PP25)
notes: R02 lands here — the seal exists and is failing. The wrongness and the anomalous ruins converge into a single crisis. Lord Gavran first named — do not over-explain him. The facility does the characterization: what he built, how he organized it, what he kept. Desh's intelligence-operative instinct should read the architecture as military command-and-control; his professional reading carries weight Ben respects. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, narrate what the seal is. He reads the words; the meaning has not reached him yet. The reader should feel the weight of SEAL FAILING land before Ben is ready to name what it protects against. Rotate the Force-wrongness metaphor for this scene: do not use the handrail or the note-played-flat line; this scene's register is denser pressure, a weight on the chest, not timing or navigation.
